definitions.explanation: To physically place objects on top of each other in layers.
To gradually gather or amass things over time, especially abstract things like experience, effort, or achievements.

examples.japanese: {本|ほん}を{積|つ}み{重|かさ}ねた。
{段|だん}ボール{箱|ばこ}を{積|つ}み{重|かさ}ねて{収納|しゅうのう}した。
examples.english: I stacked the cardboard boxes for storage.

examples.japanese: レンガを{丁寧|ていねい}に{積|つ}み{重|かさ}ねて{壁|かべ}を{作|つく}った。
examples.english: I carefully stacked the bricks to build a wall.

examples.japanese: {経験|けいけん}を{積|つ}み{重|かさ}ねることが{大切|たいせつ}だ。
{長年|ながねん}の{努力|どりょく}を{積|つ}み{重|かさ}ねて、やっと{成功|せいこう}した。
examples.english: After accumulating years of effort, I finally succeeded.

examples.japanese: {小|ちい}さな{実績|じっせき}を{積|つ}み{重|かさ}ねることで、{周囲|しゅうい}の{信頼|しんらい}を{得|え}た。
examples.english: By building up small achievements, I earned the trust of those around me.

notes:
USAGE: {積|つ}み{重|かさ}ねる is a compound verb combining {積|つ}む (to pile) and {重|かさ}ねる (to stack, to repeat). The figurative use (sense 2) is more common than the literal use.

TRANSITIVITY: Transitive ({他動詞|たどうし}). Takes を for the object being accumulated.

ASPECT: {積|つ}み{重|かさ}ねている indicates ongoing accumulation or a state of having accumulated over time.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{努力|どりょく}を{積|つ}み{重|かさ}ねる (to accumulate effort)
・{経験|けいけん}を{積|つ}み{重|かさ}ねる (to build up experience)
・{実績|じっせき}を{積|つ}み{重|かさ}ねる (to build up achievements)
・{練習|れんしゅう}を{積|つ}み{重|かさ}ねる (to accumulate practice)

RELATED: The intransitive form {積|つ}み{重|かさ}なる means "to pile up" or "to accumulate" naturally without an agent.
